I: › [ I ] to move or make progress so slowly that you are behind other people or things

T: › [ T ] to cover something with a thick layer of material in order to stop heat from escaping or to stop water from freezing
（為保溫而）覆蓋，（爲防止結冰而）給…加保溫層
› [ T ] Australian English informal to send someone to prison or to arrest someone

C: › a delay between two things happening
› UK old-fashioned informal a prisoner or a person who has often been a prisoner in the past

example: He's lagging behind - I think we'd better wait for him to catch us up.
他有點脫隊了——我看我們最好等他趕上來。
Sales are lagging at the moment.
You have to allow for a time lag between order and delivery.
訂貨和送貨之間要有一段時間間隔。

NONE: › a type of beer that is pale in colour and usually contains a lot of bubbles

example: Two pints of lager and a packet of crisps, please.
來兩品脫淡啤酒和一包炸薯片。

NONE: › a young man whose behaviour is noisy, offensive, and often violent after drinking too much alcohol
酒後行為不端的年輕人，耍酒瘋的青年
› someone or something that is very slow
行動遲緩的人；緩慢移動的事物
› a thick layer of material used to cover pipes, water tanks (= large containers), and other surfaces in order to stop heat from escaping or water from freezing
› A laggy computer, computer game, or internet connection is slow to react.
（電腦、電腦遊戲、網路）反應慢的

example: Online play is really laggy on this.
這台機器玩網路遊戲很慢。

NONE: › an area of sea water separated from the sea by a reef (= a line of rocks and sand)
